rivals.name: Sunsama
rivals.thesis: Sunsama is a paid daily planner that pulls tasks from your work tools onto a calendar, with weekly objectives and a guided weekly review, stored in US data centers. Glyph Omega starts from your mission, values and goals by area of life, kept as plain files in your vault.
short: Sunsama has no free plan. Omega is free.
Sunsama plans the work week from your calendar and tools. Omega plans from goals across every area of life.
Sunsama stores data on its US servers with an account. Omega keeps files in your vault, with no account.
rivals.pick: Pick Sunsama if your day lives in Asana, Jira, Gmail and your calendar and you want them pulled into one timeboxed plan, on Windows and Android too.

price: No free plan. $17 a month billed yearly, $22 monthly
platforms: Mac, Windows, Linux, iPhone, iPad, Android
account: Required: email, Google or Microsoft sign-in
goals: Weekly objectives and a guided weekly review
storage: Sunsama servers in US data centers (Google Cloud, AWS)
export: All data as JSON from the app

rivals.name: Todoist
rivals.thesis: Todoist is a cloud task manager on almost every device, with daily and weekly task-count goals and Karma points. Glyph Omega ties each next action to a goal, a value and an area of life, kept as files in your vault.
short: Todoist goals count tasks done. Omega goals are outcomes broken down to a next action.
Todoist needs an account and stores data on AWS. Omega has no account.
Todoist runs on Windows, Android and watches. Omega runs on Mac and iPhone.
rivals.pick: Pick Todoist if you want a fast, proven task list on every platform, shared projects with other people, and a free plan to start.

price: Free plan. Pro $5 a month billed yearly, $7 monthly
platforms: Mac, Windows, Linux, iPhone, iPad, Android, Apple Watch, Wear OS
account: Required: you must log in, even to work offline
goals: Daily and weekly task-count goals, streaks and Karma
storage: Todoist servers on AWS, encrypted at rest
offline: Yes, changes sync when back online
export: CSV per project. Auto backups on Pro

rivals.name: Notion
rivals.thesis: Notion is a cloud workspace of pages and databases; goals and weekly reviews come from templates you build or install. Glyph Omega has mission, values, goals and the weekly review built in, as plain files in your vault.
short: Notion is a blank workspace you shape. Omega is built for one job: goals down to next actions.
Notion stores workspaces on AWS, in the US by default. Omega keeps files in your vault.
Notion offline needs pages downloaded first on the free plan. Omega files are always on your device.
rivals.pick: Pick Notion if you want one flexible workspace for notes, docs and databases, shared with a team, and are happy to build or pick a goals template.

price: Free plan. Plus $10 a member a month
account: Required: you sign in with an email
goals: Through templates, such as goal trackers and weekly reviews
storage: Notion servers on AWS, US by default
offline: Desktop and mobile. Free plan: pages you choose to download
export: Markdown, CSV and HTML. PDF for single pages

rivals.note: Notion is retiring PDF export for a whole workspace; single pages still export as PDF.

rivals.name: Things 3
rivals.thesis: Things 3 is a one-time-purchase task manager for Apple devices, with Areas and Projects and a local database that syncs through Things Cloud. Glyph Omega adds mission, values, goals and a weekly review, and keeps everything as plain files in your vault.
short: Things is a paid app per device. Omega is free.
Things has Areas and Projects. Omega adds goals and a weekly review.
Things stores a database file. Omega stores plain files you can read in any editor.
rivals.pick: Pick Things 3 if you want a polished task list on Mac, iPhone, iPad, Apple Watch and Vision Pro, paid once, with no subscription.

price: One-time purchase per platform, price set on the App Store. 15-day trial
platforms: Mac, iPhone, Apple Watch, iPad, Vision Pro
account: None for one device. Free Things Cloud account to sync
goals: Areas and Projects. Its guide describes no goal or weekly review feature
storage: On your device, synced copy on Things Cloud, encrypted
export: Database file (SQLite) or print lists to PDF on Mac

rivals.note: Cultured Code's own pages do not list USD prices; they point to the App Store.
